Job Description:
Financial Analyst – Originations
Purpose of the role
To provide dedicated financial screening, modelling and Investment Committee preparation support for acquisition opportunities across Pallas Software Group.  The role matures the financial insights on targets, so that every Portfolio Manager has early access to rigorous, consistent analysis that can advance the PQs and Modelling before handing across to the M&A Execution team for final checking and approvals.
The role sits within the Finance function already attached to the Pallas Portfolio, working across all Portfolio Managers. The resource is deployed flexibly to whichever Portfolio Manager has a live origination or diligence need at a given time, working under the direction of the Finance Director to prioritise across competing demands.
Scope of Coverage
• Verticals: all software verticals held across the Pallas Software Group portfolio. The role is not dedicated to any single vertical and takes direction from the Finance Director on where to prioritise effort.
• Geography: United Kingdom and Ireland as the core market, extending to other European geographies as individual Portfolio Managers' mandates require.
• Deal types: platform acquisitions and bolt, on acquisitions into existing business units, as directed by the relevant Portfolio Manager.
• Deal size: predominantly owner, managed and founder, led businesses below the size threshold that attracts a competitive banked process.
Key Responsibilities
Screening and origination support
• Screen inbound and adviser, introduced opportunities, from any part of the group, against group investment criteria and hurdle rates, recommending pursue, watch, list or pass with a written rationale.
• Maintain and refresh target maps and market intelligence for the verticals each Portfolio Manager is actively assessing, using public, paid and proprietary sources.
• Support Portfolio Managers' adviser and intermediary relationships by logging opportunities promptly and coordinating timely follow, up.
• Monitor market events, funding rounds, leadership changes, competitor acquisitions and distress signals and flag relevant opportunities to the appropriate Portfolio Manager.
Modelling, analysis and execution
• Build acquisition models from source data: revenue quality and recurring revenue analysis, customer cohort and churn analysis, maintenance and net revenue retention trends, normalised EBITDA, working capital, cash conversion, IRR and payback under base, downside and upside cases.
• Prepare Investment Committee papers and offer support material, investment thesis, valuation range and bridge, key risks, integration assumptions and returns scenarios.
• Support the central execution team and Portfolio Managers in coordinating due diligence workstreams across finance, legal, technical and people contributors; maintain the diligence tracker and issues log; translate findings into model and price adjustments.
• Support deal structuring: consideration split, earn, out mechanics and metric definition, deferred consideration, escrow and set, off, and operational ring, fence provisions.
• Track post, completion performance against the acquisition model and feed variances back into future underwriting, across all portfolios the role has supported.
Pipeline management and reporting.
• Own pipeline management jointly with the BD Manager: the BD Manager owns origination and outreach volume, this role owns the financial qualification and status of each target, and the two work from a shared, current view of the pipeline.
• Own the capturing of notes and information recorded in the group CRM, on behalf of whichever Portfolio Manager the work relates to.
• Produce a standing pipeline report for the Portfolio and Finance Director covering coverage by vertical and geography, stage conversion rates, and pipeline ageing across the group.
• Maintain a competitive and valuation reference set spanning the verticals in which the group is active.
Person Specification
Essential
• Minimum of 2 years experience in a financial analysis role with direct exposure to M&A: transaction services, corporate development, lower midmarket M&A, or growth/debt finance
• Genuine modelling capability — able to build an acquisition model from messy management accounts and a trial balance without a template, and to defend the assumptions in front of an Investment Committee.
• Understanding of software business economics: recurring revenue, retention and expansion, gross margin structure, implementation and services drag, and hosting costs.
• Comfortable working across multiple stakeholders and priorities at once, taking direction from the Finance Director on where to focus effort at any given time.
• Credible with a Portfolio Manager and a founder's finance director in the same week. Writes clearly and concisely.
• Self, directing, with sound judgement on when to escalate and when to proceed.

The Chief Security Office helps us move fast without compromising security, resilience or control.

We are seeking a commercially astute Risk Assessment & Pricing Specialist (actuarial, analytical, modelling or reinsurance pricing background) to build technical capability and scale global growth.
At MS Amlin, Sustainability is integral to how we grow profitably and responsibly, balancing business value with societal impact and the environment. Our goal is to make resilience insurable, scalable and commercially sustainable. This role suits someone who enjoys collaborating on complex risks while contributing to profitable growth and positive impact.
This role will act as the dedicated risk assessment and pricing capability for ESG Re and will be closely aligned with the Actuarial Pricing team. You will support the Head of Sustainability, ESG Re team, and Reinsurance function, applying structured analysis to emerging market risks, where insurance affordability and availability remain limited.
You will combine quantitative analysis with commercial judgment, supporting new revenue streams and deliver commercially grounded solutions. The role contributes to closing the global protection gap while enabling resilience and long-term value creation.
About the Job
As a Risk & Pricing Specialist, you’ll be at the forefront of supporting underwriting with technically robust, commercially informed insights, particularly across innovative resilience and adaptation solutions, spanning climate change, nature loss, evolving global health, conflict and migration and other systemic risks. While no two days are alike, here’s a snapshot of key responsibilities:
• Assess technical submissions spanning climate, nature, health, conflict & systemic risks, including exposure evaluation, structure review, expected loss estimation & rate-on-line guidance.
• Analyse data to build robust, transparent risk assessments & pricing approaches that support business objectives & enable scalable, commercially viable solutions.
• Challenge data, assumptions, catastrophe outputs & pricing methodologies to ensure technical rigour & alignment with MS Amlin’s view of risk and its Sustainability Strategy.
• Act as a trusted technical advisor to the Head of Sustainability & Senior Underwriters, offering insight into expected loss calculations, pricing & renewal considerations, and treaty and portfolio structures including layer terms, loss histories & accumulation
• Translate unconventional or development-driven proposals into clear, insurable structures with disciplined pricing, strengthening ESG Re's ability to convert pipeline opportunities into bound business.
• Support the ESG Re Team in structuring innovative products (parametric, index-based, blended-finance-backed, sovereign risk pools, community schemes) that support adaptation finance and inclusive growth.
• Support market engagement by preparing technical insights for discussions with brokers, multilaterals, NGOs & humanitarians; help articulate our pricing rationale, risk appetite & product value propositions in the context of systemic risk reduction.
• Work cross-functionally across pricing, model development, data improvement and wider Sustainability initiatives.

• Have an entrepreneurial mindset and are excited by building new markets, not just operating in established ones.
• Have a passion for problem-solving and interrogating complex, unconventional datasets.
• Collaborate naturally across underwriting, actuarial, modelling, and analytics functions with the aim of improving technical processes, models and approaches.

Essential:
• Experience in (re)insurance pricing, risk analysis, catastrophe modelling, or reinsurance underwriting.
• Strong capability in interpreting complex datasets, evaluating reinsurance structures and performing technical risk assessments.
• Confidence in challenging assumptions, pricing methodologies and modelled and non modelled outputs in emerging or data constrained environments.
• Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders.
• Strong time management and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-moving environment.
• Working knowledge of catastrophe modelling, climate risk analytics, or parametric product design (including their limitations in emerging markets and developing economies).
• Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences, including external partners such as NGOs, development banks and governments.
Desirable:

• Strong scientific, actuarial, data science, statistics or equivalent technical/analytical background (degree, PhD or equivalent).
• Experience in reinsurance treaty underwriting, portfolio management or structuring non-traditional risk transfer solutions.
• Experience leading complex projects aligned to strategic business objectives and partnering with diverse stakeholders across the resilience value chain.
• Proficiency in at least one analytical or modelling language (SQL, Python, R, VBA).

You will lead our responsible deployment agenda for AVEVA’s AI software products and for adoption of AI within AVEVA’s operations.  Our responsible AI agenda is grounded in a set of core principles: sustainability; accuracy and robustness; human-centricity and fairness; data governance and privacy; transparency and explainability; and accountability.
A key aspect of the role is translating these principles into practical guidance, governance frameworks, learning programmes and deployment standards, helping build a shared understanding of what Responsible AI means for AVEVA, our customers and our stakeholders.
Responsible deployment is core to AVEVA’s Industrial AI agenda, and this role will balance external engagement with internal governance. Externally, you will work with customers, industry bodies, standards organisations, and public sector stakeholders to shape practical governance and accountability approaches for safe, secure, and sustainable AI in industrial operations, across regulated, safety- and mission-critical industrial environments. Internally, you will help to convert those expectations into scalable policies, controls, and decision processes that product and engineering teams can adopt.
You will partner closely with our Product, Enterprise IT, Security, Sustainability, Legal, Risk and Talent and Learning teams, while remaining accountable for responsible deployment in policy design, stakeholder engagement, and enterprise learning enablement.

• Industry and standards participation: Represent the company in relevant forums (industry working groups, standards bodies and multi-stakeholder initiatives). Contribute practical input on accountability, assurance and deployment patterns grounded in industrial realities.
• External narratives and materials: Develop external-facing guidance (whitepapers, position notes, playbooks and customer assurance packets) to explain how we deploy AI responsibly and how customers can operationalise governance.
• Embed governance into product delivery: Partner with R&D/Portfolio to integrate governance into product delivery systems.

• Metrics and continuous improvement: Establish KPIs (e.g., deployment readiness, exceptions, time-to-remediate, control coverage) and feed lessons from customer engagements back into internal standards.
• Stakeholder Engagement and Policy Advocacy: Actively engage with industry groups, regulatory bodies and technology partners to advocate for responsible AI practices. Represent the organisation in external forums to share insights, learn from global best practices and contribute to the evolution of Responsible AI governance and policy.
B) AVEVA Operations
• Support the responsible adoption, procurement, deployment and use of AI across AVEVA’s operations in line with AVEVA’s Responsible AI Principles.
• Provide guidance to business leaders and AI initiatives on balancing innovation, productivity, regulatory expectations, risk management and responsible outcomes.
• Identify emerging risks, governance gaps and adoption challenges associated with enterprise AI use and develop practical mitigation approaches.
Essential Requirements

CrowdStrike Falcon Host is a two-component security product. One component is a “sensor”, which is a driver installed on client machines that observes system activity and recognizes malicious behavior, then provides on-box prevention capability and remote telemetry to the Falcon Host cloud. The cloud component aggregates sensor telemetry for each customer’s network can correlate malicious behavior across multiple machines and presents our customers’ operations teams with a prioritized summary of the threats detected in their environments.

You will be required to assist with architecting solutions and support in implementing our core features. Features will cross-cut most core OS subsystems such as file system, memory and process, and networking.

Who are we? We are EDF Trading, part of the EDF Group - a world leader in low-carbon, sustainable electricity generation.
Join us, make a difference, and help shape the future of energy.
Job Description:
Department
The Short-Term Analytical Team
Position purpose
The role is based in London. In order for EDF Trading to maximise the return from the month-ahead to day-ahead wholesale power markets, either from EDF generation assets or through proprietary trading, the traders require detailed, commercially focussed analysis produced on a timely basis.
In the front office, working closely with both the short-term analysts in charge of EDF portfolio optimisation in Paris and the power traders in London, the Short-Term Power Market Analyst has a dual role covering both operational and development duties.
Moreover, the analyst is expected to take distance from the operational activity and our modelling in order to identify areas of improvement and contribute to the definition of the objectives of the team. He/She must participate to the training of junior analysts.
Main Operational Responsibilities
Market Analysis:
• Provide data analytics and risk analysis on short term power market to the desk
• Support the Short-Term desk for the price forecasts and trading strategies
EDF system risk analysis:
• Follow the Day-Ahead and Week-Ahead optimisation shifts
• Communicate time critical information to the traders in London
• Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, including REMIT, through the consistent application of defined processes.
Main Development/Modelling Responsibilities
The short-term power market analyst is responsible of the whole life cycle of an application or a model: from the research/design to the development/implementation and the maintenance.
The analyst is autonomous on his/her projects and is responsible of critical applications.
Example of models/applications/solutions:
• Fundamental and quantitative (statistical, data science driven) models to better anticipate market behaviour and improve price forecasting models. All components of the market could be addressed like load forecast, competitors’ orders, availabilities, etc...
• Automation of workflows
• Data visualisation via powerBI or web applications
The analyst is also responsible in improving robustness of the applications of the team by adding unit tests on critical parts of the applications and refactoring unstable functions he/she uses in his projects. The analyst must take part actively to the peer reviews of the junior analysts in order to share good practises.
Experience required
Ability to work under pressure, timeliness, accuracy and the ability to understand the wider commercial implications of the work are critical to be successful in this position.
The analyst will use his/her expertise to support the short-term power traders while at the same time ensuring an effective operational relationship with the asset managers at EDF. He/she will be expected to take the initiative to continuously improve existing processes, tools and models with the aim of improving the overall management of the EDF portfolio and wholesale market positions.
It is as well necessary to be proactive in the research of market modelling improvements to succeed in this position.
Technical requirements
Fluent in French & English
Educated to master’s degree level, preferably with a high statistics or mathematics component
Experience of building/developing stochastic or deterministic optimisation procedures/models
Advanced skills in:
• Data science
• Python (Api, Data management, statistical modelling)
• Web development (javascript)
• Source code management (Git)
Full understanding of the ways of working of the power market:
• Power asset management and optimisation
• Power market coupling algorithm
Person specification
As well as having strong analytical skills, attention to detail and enthusiasm the candidate needs to have a commercial approach to his/her duties. Similarly, a flexible approach to problem solving and the ability to work under pressure are essential.
Applicants for the role will also be expected to have strong communications skills with the confidence to work effectively with both power traders and asset managers.
Hours of work:
40 hours per week, Monday to Friday

kla.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/search/job/new.description_excerpt:
To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
Group/Division
KLA has manufacturing sites worldwide. The Global Operations (GOPS) team, comprised of Manufacturing, Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing Engineering, Installation and Quality, builds our leading-edge technology. GOPS partners with KLA's global supply base and design engineering teams to develop new products, working continuously to build better, faster and more cost-efficient solutions.
What You'll Do
In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
At KLA SensArray, we manufacture highly specialised semiconductor metrology & inspection equipment used by leading semiconductor manufacturers worldwide. Based at our state-of-the-art facility in Newport, South Wales, this role offers the opportunity to work in a clean, precision manufacturing environment where attention to detail and craftsmanship are critical to product quality.
As the dedicated Quality Control (QC) Technician you will provide independent quality inspection and verification across the SensArray manufacturing process, covering incoming materials, in-process production activity, and final outgoing product release.
The role is responsible for ensuring that products, components, substrates, documentation, cleanliness standards, meet defined requirements before progressing through production.
Your Day-to-Day Responsibilities
Incoming Quality Control
• Inspect incoming materials, substrates, components, consumables, and supplier documentation against defined specifications.
• Confirm correct part numbers, revision levels, quantities, packaging condition, and traceability requirements.
• Identify, quarantine, and escalate non-conforming or suspect material before release to production.
• Maintain accurate incoming inspection records and support supplier quality follow-up where required.
In-Process Quality Control
• Perform quality checks across SensArray production lines, including High Temp, Etch Temp, TC, RTD, and DISIS, to confirm products and processes meet applicable standards.
• Verify operators are working on current SOPs, work instructions, process controls, and quality requirements.
• Conduct routine quality gates, process audits, and workmanship checks during key manufacturing stages.
• Monitor ESD, cleanliness, documentation, and product handling standards across the production area.
• Support containment activity and stop escalation when quality risks are identified.
Outgoing Quality Control
• Complete final inspection of finished products before shipment.
• Review product quality records, test data, manufacturing documentation, labelling, and traceability.
• Confirm products meet customer, internal, packaging, and shipping requirements before release.
• Approve, reject, or escalate product release decisions based on inspection outcome.
Non-Conformance & Quality Improvement
• Raise and support Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs) for identified defects or process failures.
• Assist with containment, root cause investigation, corrective action, and preventive action activity.
• Track recurring issues, quality trends, and defect data to support continuous improvement.
• Work with Production, Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain teams to reduce risk and improve process capability.
Skills & Experience
Essential
• Previous Quality Control or Quality Assurance experience within an electronics manufacturing environment.
• Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, work instructions, and quality requirements.
• Experience performing visual, dimensional, documentation, or final product inspections.
• Strong attention to detail with the confidence to challenge non-conforming work.
• Competent in Microsoft Office and ERP systems.
Desirable
• Experience in semiconductor, electronics, clean manufacturing, or high-reliability production environments.
• Knowledge of ESD controls, cleanroom practices, ISO 9001 quality systems, SPC, and quality metrics.
• Experience using microscopes, metrology equipment, or other inspection tools.
• Understanding of root cause analysis and continuous improvement methodologies.
Qualifications
• HNC qualification or equivalent technical qualification would be advantageous
What will we offer you?
This is a permanent position working Monday to Friday.
KLA benefits include - Annual leave starting at 25 days (plus bank holidays), contributory pension scheme, cash health plan, cycle to work scheme, global bonus plan, share scheme, rewards scheme, life assurance and overtime premiums.
Minimum Qualifications
About KLA
We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.
Use of AI Statement
At KLA, our interviews seek to understand your individual skills, problem-solving approach and authentic thinking. To ensure a fair and consistent evaluation, the use of AI, recording tools or other technologies to generate, suggest or provide responses during interviews—whether virtual or in person—is not permitted unless explicitly approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation or invited by the interviewer. Use of these tools may interfere with our ability to evaluate your individual qualifications and affect your candidacy. KLA is committed to advancing innovation through responsible AI, and we value candidates who share this mindset.

We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it.
Bristol Myers Squibb | European Tax Centre of Excellence
•

• Family cover healthcare
• Attractive contributory pension scheme
• Hybrid working, 50% home / 50% office, giving you flexibility and balance
• 26 days holiday, plus bank holidays, plus festive shutdown

What if your tax expertise could do more than manage compliance — what if it could help change patients' lives?
It might not be the first thing that comes to mind when you think about a tax role but at Bristol Myers Squibb, everything connects back to our purpose: transforming patients' lives through science. And the team that keeps our tax operations running with precision and integrity? They're part of that story too.
We're looking for a Senior Tax Manager to join our European Tax Centre of Excellence (COE) in Chester - a role where your technical skills meet real business influence and where the work you do every day genuinely matters.
This is a tax role with real breadth. And real accountability for the outcomes across your markets.
Here's what makes this different from a standard in-house tax position: you won't be a cog in a machine, processing the same returns year after year.
You'll lead a portfolio of European markets and direct a team of tax professionals - working closely with local finance teams and external advisers to high-quality processes. You'll be the expert your finance colleagues come to when they need clarity, the professional who challenges external advisers on both direct tax and VAT matters, the senior lead who manages tax audits through to resolution, and the person who translates complex legislation into practical action to guide our stakeholders
Here's what your role will actually look like:
• You'll run the full direct tax cycle for your own markets - leading corporate income tax return preparation with local external advisers, applying genuine technical challenge to their work, managing tax authority audits and enquiries through to resolution, drawing on your working knowledge of VAT where indirect tax questions arise, and making sure nothing falls through the cracks.
• You'll gain hands-on US GAAP experience - preparing and submitting US tax reporting including quarterly current and deferred tax provisions using TaxStream technology. This isn't something most in-house European tax roles offer, and it's a genuine differentiator for your CV.
• You'll work across the full breadth of tax governance - staying on top of evolving regulatory requirements across your markets, including the evolving world of Pillar Two.
• You'll be a genuine internal consultant - advising finance and business stakeholders on tax matters, explaining complex technical requirements in language they can act on, and building the kind of trusted relationships that make you indispensable.
• You'll coach and assist in developing a team of tax professionals - setting objectives, coaching technical development, and building a team that delivers to a consistently high standard across your markets.
• You'll shape how tax is done, not just do it - contributing to the COE's strategy around standardisation, automation, and continuous improvement. If you're curious about tax technology and smarter ways of working, this team is actively investing in that space.
• You'll stay ahead of legislative change - monitoring developments across your markets, analysing their impact, and proactively communicating what matters to the people who need to know.
What do you actually gain from joining this team?
Let's talk about what this role opens up for you - concretely.
Breadth that most tax roles simply don't offer. European direct tax, US GAAP reporting, transfer pricing exposure, Pillar Two - all under one role, in one team. Whether you're looking to deepen your specialism or broaden your horizons, this role does both.
Access to leading external advisers. You won't be working in isolation. You'll collaborate with top-tier advisory firms, learn from their expertise, and develop the skills to challenge and manage them effectively - experience that builds your professional credibility significantly.
Real stakeholder visibility. You'll regularly engage with senior finance leaders and business partners globally. That kind of cross-functional, international exposure builds commercial acumen and communication skills that go far beyond technical tax knowledge.
Flexible, hybrid working from our modern office in Chester. A. With the 50% hybrid-working model, you’ll get to collaborate and build supportive working relationships with the large tax team, as well as others in the ECC, whilst creating a healthy work-life balance.
The BMS mission as your backdrop. When you're filing that return, managing that audit, or navigating a piece of new legislation — you're doing it in support of a company that is genuinely working to help patients with serious diseases. That context changes how the work feels.
You'll thrive in this role if…
• You're a qualified accountant and/or chartered tax adviser (CTA, ACA, ACCA or equivalent) with solid experience in tax accounting, tax provisioning, and statutory audit support.
• You have hands-on tax audit experience, having led or managed enquiries with tax authorities, and a good working knowledge of VAT.
• You have experience coaching and developing people, with a track record of managing, coaching and growing tax professionals.
• You've managed external advisers and you know how to review compliance deliverables with the right level of technical rigour.
• You communicate confidently - able to break down complex tax matters for finance colleagues and non-tax stakeholders alike, without losing accuracy.
• You're genuinely interested in tax technology, process improvement, and automation and you see them as opportunities, not threats.
• You're organised, ownership-driven, and comfortable managing multiple markets and deadlines simultaneously.
• You're fluent in English - additional European languages are a bonus, but not a requirement.
Don't tick every single box? We'd still love to hear from you. If you believe you could succeed in this role, that matters to us and we mean it.

We are uniquely positioned to become a world leader in SMR technology and one of the UK’s most exciting green export opportunities—combining proven nuclear engineering with advanced modular manufacturing to transform how low‑carbon power is delivered.
The Team
You’ll be joining the Materials & Chemistry team. This cross‑functional group supports the entire lifecycle of the RR‑SMR—from concept design to decommissioning—providing essential expertise across Reactor Plant & Systems, Components & Mechanical Equipment, Manufacturing Engineering, the Conventional Island, and both internal and external supply chain stakeholders. Your contribution will help shape the safety, integrity, and performance of the SMR design.
Role Summary
We are recruiting a Senior Materials Engineer – Welding & Manufacturing, a key technical role responsible for developing, assuring, and integrating the welding and manufacturing requirements that underpin the RR‑SMR design. This role is essential to ensuring that all structural materials, welds, special processes, and manufacturing routes meet our expectations for nuclear‑grade integrity. You will act as a technical partner to our supply chain, and a trusted advisor within multidisciplinary engineering teams. Your contribution will significantly influence compliance, manufacturability, and long‑term plant safety.
Key Responsibilities
You will be doing…
•
Leading the development and delivery of material specifications and providing expert manufacturing support.
•
Acting as technical partner for suppliers who design and manufacture metallic components—reviewing and approving Methods of Manufacture, documentation packs, data cards, and final documentation.
•
Supporting the design and welding teams on weld consumable specification, supply, and control.

Conducting or supporting special process audits (such as heat treatment, forging, welding) and maintaining oversight of supplier special processes and non‑conformance resolution.
•
Collaborating closely with internal engineering and project stakeholders, representing RR‑SMR with suppliers and industry bodies.

In this role, you will directly contribute to the integrity and manufacturability of the RR‑SMR’s key components. A degree (or equivalent) in a relevant engineering discipline (materials, welding, mechanical, manufacturing, etc.).

Strong understanding of materials systems, their behaviour, and intended nuclear uses.

Practical experience in materials manufacturing, including interpretation of manufacturing routes, special process controls, forging, fabrication, welding, post‑weld heat treatment, and documentation packs.

Experience supporting or conducting technical audits of special processes.

Experience working in a regulated industry, ideally nuclear or power generation. (Experience with PWR environments, ALARP/BAT, and ASME compliance beneficial.)

Strong communication skills and proven ability to present technical information clearly to diverse stakeholders.

We anticipate paying a salary of between £50,650 - £66,500 plus:-

Help grow a safer, cleaner, healthier future for everyone, every day.
Job Title: Lead Software Engineer – Hardware Lifecycle
Reports to: Head of Digital Delivery
Location: Hybrid, on-site 1 day per week (with more as needed) in Cwmbran, Wales.
Job Type: Permanent
About Us
We are a pioneer in network infrastructure monitoring with IoT technology, and develop innovations that keep critical resources flowing for water and wastewater utilities. Our customers operate large fleets of our sensors and dataloggers, with tens or hundreds of thousands of devices. Good software is critical to managing those fleets.
About the Role
The Hardware Lifecycle team is responsible for the software that enables HWM and our customers to manage device fleets at every stage of their lifecycle: deliver, deploy, run and renew.
We're looking for an experienced Lead Software Engineer to lead the transformation of this software. Our strategy is to focus on three core products:
• An installation and deployment app, used by field engineers (mobile)
• A fleet monitoring cloud application for internal use (Ruby on Rails)
• A customer fleet administration cloud application (C# .NET and React)
Today we have five. Two existing mobile apps need to be combined and rationalised into the single installation and deployment app, and a legacy desktop application will receive maintenance changes only until our support commitments end. Leading the team to that target state, and making these three products a genuine differentiator for HWM, is the core of this role.
The role also carries a significant element of product ownership. You'll work closely with Product Management and the Head of Digital Delivery, but we're looking for someone self-driven who takes real ownership of the product. With the support of a designer, you'll get close to customers and field engineers, understand their problems and turn that into clear direction for the team, rather than working through tickets defined elsewhere.
You'll lead three direct reports. The team is deliberately small, with a focused set of three products and extensive use of AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code.
The team sits within our wider Digital team, alongside several similarly shaped teams working on other priority areas. These teams share knowledge, help each other out and form tiger teams when a problem needs it, so you won't be working in isolation.
This is a hands-on leadership role. We expect up to 40% of your time to be spent coding, varying with the phase of work, so you'll keep your technical skills sharp while leading the team.
Key Objectives for the first 12 months
• Deliver measurable improvements in fleet operations, such as faster provisioning and deployment, and fewer support requests per thousand devices
• Agree a roadmap and target architecture for consolidating onto the three core products
• Evaluate the mobile platform options (.NET MAUI and Flutter), make a recommendation and begin delivering the combined installation and deployment app on the chosen platform
• Build on the team's existing use of AI-assisted development to make it a core strength, and use it to accelerate the modernisation of our legacy code
Responsibilities
• Lead the Hardware Lifecycle software team, providing technical guidance, mentorship and coaching, and improving team processes
• Own the technical direction and architecture of the team's software, and clearly articulate engineering trade-offs to technical and non-technical colleagues
• Act as product owner, working with Product Management, customers and colleagues across the business to shape and prioritise the backlog, and take responsibility for the outcomes delivered
• Manage legacy applications through to end of support, limiting changes to essential maintenance
• Design, develop and maintain high-quality software across our tech stack (C# .NET, React, Xamarin/.NET MAUI, Ruby on Rails, Azure, Git)
• Support our move from a Windows-centric environment to a more platform-agnostic approach, including Linux
• Identify and mitigate technical risks, and develop strategies to address technical debt
• Provide responsive support for urgent user issues
Role Requirements
Leadership Skills
• Proven experience of leading a software team, including:
• Experience of leading a team through a legacy modernisation or re-platforming
• A strong sense of product ownership, with experience of shaping requirements and priorities rather than only implementing them
• Excellent communication skills, with stakeholders and team members alike
• A cool head with excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills
Technical Skills
• Significant experience in software development, with strong C# .NET skills
• Experience of mobile app development (Xamarin, .NET MAUI or Flutter) and web development, ideally React
• Open-minded and willing to work across multiple technology stacks, including those new to you
• Regular, hands-on use of AI-assisted development tools
• Experience with Linux as well as Windows environments
• Familiarity with cloud-based services, especially Azure, and security fundamentals
• Experience with CI/CD pipelines, Git and automated testing
• Significant experience with RDBMS and SQL
Desirable
• Experience with Flutter/Dart or Ruby on Rails
• Experience of IoT, device management or fleet/asset management systems
• Experience in the utilities or critical infrastructure sector
• Personal or open-source projects outside of work (links welcome with your application)
What we Offer
37.5 hours per week with core working hours and flexible options. Benefits include 26 days of annual leave plus bank holidays, the option to buy or sell holidays, a pension plan with employer contribution up to 10.5%, a salary sacrifice car scheme, health coverage, parental leave, and an employee assistance programme. #HWM

• Experience troubleshooting complex network issues, including packet analysis using tools such as tcpdump, Wireshark, tshark, or similar

• Experience with scripting and/or API-driven automation to improve operational efficiency and reduce manual effort

Please only apply for one internship position, choosing the role that best matches your skills and interests. We'll consider your application across all of our research opportunities where appropriate.
We tackle the most complex problems in quantitative finance, by bringing scientific clarity to financial complexity.
From our London HQ, we unite world-class researchers and engineers in an environment that values deep exploration and methodical execution - because the best ideas take time to evolve.  Together we’re building a world-class platform to amplify our teams’ most powerful ideas.
Join a research team where curiosity meets scale. You’ll investigate foundational questions, uncover market insights and push the boundaries of what's possible - all with the support of near-limitless compute and world-class peers.
Take the next step in your career.
The role
• 10-week summer programme (21st June - 27th August 2027)
• 09:00-17:30 working hours
• Based in Central London
Over the course of 10 weeks, G-Research Summer Research Programme interns gain a unique insight into life as a Quantitative Researcher at a leading quantitative finance research firm.
You will be given a meaningful and challenging research project that demands the application of innovative yet pragmatic mathematical and computational analysis.
Using rigorous scientific methodology, robust statistical analysis and pattern recognition, you will extract meaningful predictive signals from financial time-series and use these to predict future dynamics.
Your project will give you the opportunity to use a wide range of techniques in areas such as mathematical modelling, deep learning, optimisation and machine learning in a practical and challenging context. Additional work may involve the implementation of back-testing frameworks to ensure signal robustness or the creation of a pipeline which constructs and simulates the performance of a portfolio derived from various input signals.
Throughout the internship, you will collaborate closely with a Quantitative Researcher who will mentor you as you complete your independent project. You will receive structured feedback and reviews to help you to improve and develop, culminating in a final presentation of your research ideas to senior management.
Taking part in G-Research's Summer Internship Programme will give you an in-depth insight into our academic approach to quantitative finance. You will also have the opportunity to explore London and get to know your fellow interns and colleagues through a full itinerary of social events.
Top performers on the internship will be considered for full-time opportunities on completion of their studies.
Who are we looking for?
The ideal candidate will have the following skills and experience:
• Strong mathematical background
• Intermediate level of programming in at least one object-oriented language, ideally Python or C#
• Interest in applying data science, machine learning and optimisation techniques to real-world problems
• Be in the final or penultimate year of a Masters or PhD in a highly technical or quantitative subject such as Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, Engineering or Computer Science, with a PhD preferred
• Active GitHub or Kaggle profiles are desirable but not essential
• Previous experience in finance is not required, but an interest in finance and a willingness to learn are essential
Why should you apply?
• Highly competitive compensation plus accommodation
• G-Research community with weekly intern activities
• Lunch provided (via Just Eat for Business) and dedicated barista bar
• 30 days’ annual leave pro-rated
• Informal dress code and excellent work/life balance
• Central London office close to 5 stations and 6 tube lines

About Mimecast
The work people build is worth protecting, and it's harder to protect than it used to be. Overview
Customer Development is looking for a Senior Sales Manager to lead, coach and develop a team of Commercial Account Managers responsible for protecting and growing revenue across Mimecast's existing customer base in EMEA. This is a high-velocity, data-led sales environment focused on upselling our expanding product portfolio, mitigating downsell and churn, and driving incremental growth.
Reporting to the Director, Customer Development EMEA, you'll be a customer-centric sales leader who delivers against quota through others. You'll establish a disciplined, evidence-based operating rhythm—rigorously inspecting pipeline, forecasting accurately, coaching live deals and holding the team to a consistent sales methodology—while developing talent and building strong customer and partner relationships.
This role is based from Mimecast's London, UK headquarters, with a minimum of two days per week in the office and travel for customer and account reviews throughout the year.
What You'll Do
• Own and deliver the team's monthly, quarterly and annual upsell revenue targets across the assigned book of business, while actively managing downsell, churn and net revenue retention.
• Drive sales of new technology into the existing customer base, identifying cross-sell, whitespace, account-penetration and incremental growth opportunities.
• Build and execute territory and account plans in partnership with Channel and Partner Development teams.
• Deliver accurate rolling six-month forecasts for upsell, downsell and churn, maintaining clear commit and best-case discipline at representative and team level.
• Run structured bi-weekly pipeline inspections, identifying stalled opportunities, testing qualification and driving clear next steps.
• Maintain strong CRM discipline and analyse week-over-week pipeline movement—including stage changes, close-date pushes, forecast changes and ARR movement—to identify and address risk early.
• Embed an end-to-end sales methodology and qualification framework, using call intelligence and CRM data to coach live opportunities and address the root causes of deal slippage.
• Set clear performance goals and lead a consistent coaching cadence through weekly one-to-ones, team meetings and enablement sessions.
• Attract, retain, train and motivate a diverse, high-performing team, developing talent from within and inspiring performance through words and actions.
• Build strong relationships with key customers, partners and cross-functional stakeholders, while providing accurate KPI reporting and management information to leadership.
What You'll Bring
• Demonstrable IT or SaaS sales and people-leadership experience, with the ability to lead direct, indirect and remote sales teams to revenue targets; experience in email, messaging, security or storage is helpful but not essential.
• A proven record of achieving revenue quota through others in a high-velocity, customer-focused commercial environment.
• Strong data literacy and forecasting rigor, with the ability to interrogate CRM and pipeline analytics—such as Salesforce and Snowflake dashboards—to inspect deals and drive decisions.
• Fluency in a recognised sales methodology and qualification framework, such as Force Management, MEDDPICC or similar, and the ability to embed it consistently across a team.
• Strong pipeline-management instincts, including the ability to identify risk early, maintain healthy coverage and lead accurate commit and best-case calls.
• An emotionally intelligent, coaching-led leadership style that sets clear expectations, holds people accountable and develops talent.
• Strong business and commercial acumen, including an understanding of corporate IT teams and buying processes.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across functions and build credibility with customers and partners.
• A resilient, customer-centric and results-oriented approach, with the confidence and humility to operate in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
• Degree-level education is preferred but not required.
• Eligibility to work in the UK and the ability to work from Mimecast's London headquarters at least two days per week.

About CRFS
CRFS, part of Motorola Solutions, is a world leader in radio frequency (RF) technology, providing mission-critical solutions for defence, national security, and regulatory agencies. Our RFeye ecosystem - including ruggedized sensors, direction-finding arrays, and advanced software suites - allows our customers to detect, identify, and geolocate signals of interest in the most complex electromagnetic environments. We operate at the cutting edge of spectrum dominance, electronic warfare, and signal intelligence.
The Role
We have an opportunity for a Senior Software Product Manager to bridge the gap between complex engineering capabilities and real-world customer missions. This is not a "pure" product management role; it also requires some technical understanding of embedded and application software, as well as familiarity with electronic systems for RF mission applications.
You will be the "voice of the system", working closely with our engineering teams to develop innovative solutions to high-stakes problems. You will take ownership for some of our software products (both current and future), ensuring they not only have clear development roadmaps, but also solve the challenges faced by our global customer base and are the best they can be.
Key Responsibilities
• Software Solutions: Translate customer and partner requirements into actionable software product roadmaps and specifications, working collaboratively with Senior Engineering, Sales and Product Management colleagues.
• Product Owner:  As the owner and lead for Software Products (application and embedded) you will maintain a coherent roadmap across all software components, including real-time user applications, embedded real-time, APIs, and user-interfaces.  You will develop promotional content for the marketing team, and provide occasional support at trade events.
• Product Lifecycle Management (PLM): Support the technical evolution of our RFeye products from concept through to deployment and end-of-life.  Contribute to PLM activities to ensure that RFeye products meet customer requirements, are positioned and marketed effectively and that the CRFS Sales, Customer Support and Application Engineering teams are fully equipped and trained to sell and support them.
• Bridge Engineering & Commercial: Work alongside software and systems engineers to evaluate trade-offs, ensuring that engineering efforts align with market needs and commercial viability.
• Market & Application Insight: Develop a deep understanding of use-cases, including TDOA/AOA geolocation, signal capture and analysis, and electronic warfare support.
• Hands-on Product User:  You will be expected to use our products and become proficient in their use with a view to ensuring they are the best they can be – forming your own judgement on capabilities, improvements and updates using ‘customer eyes’.  You will also engage with end users to elicit their input and feedback.
• Documentation & Training: Author high-quality white papers, requirement specifications, and user stories. Ensure the Field Application Engineering (FAE) team is fully equipped to demonstrate new system capabilities.
Basic Requirements
Required Qualifications & Experience
• Education: A degree in Engineering (software/electronic/systems preferable) or a related technical field.
• Industry Experience: 3-5+ years of experience in a technical role, ideally within Wireless/RF, Telecommunications, Defence, or Aerospace.
• Technical Literacy: Strong foundational knowledge of RF systems (receivers, antennas, signal processing) and wireless communications.
• User and Solution Mindset: Proven ability to move beyond "features" and think about customer needs and solutions - how hardware and software interact to solve a specific end-user problem.  A demonstrable ability to understand and discuss technical concepts, manage trade-offs, and evaluate opportunistic new ideas against current commitments alongside cross-functional stakeholders.
• Communication and Approach:  Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal. A positive attitude and ability to get things done, whilst being a committed team player.  An ability to build strong relationships and collaborate with colleagues and clients on product requirements and specifications.
• Product Management: While we welcome engineers looking to transition, prior experience in product management, technical sales support, or systems engineering is highly desirable.
Desirable Skills

• Understanding of deployable equipment use within a harsh or military environments and modern user interfaces.
• Familiarity with Agile development methodologies and tools like Jira.
• The ability to present complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders or customers.
• Source, compile and analyse market, voice of customer and competitor information.

Under 10%

Experienced

Job Description:
About Us
Flui Technologies is a leading software solution provider to the energy and water sector, delivering innovative and scalable software infrastructure and services since 1990. Our solutions - MarketFlow, MeterFlow and DCC adapter - support market competition, smart metering, network flexibility and supplier integration across Energy Retail, Energy Networks and Water Retail, and are used to manage messaging for more than 35 million electricity and gas meter points, with millions of records processed per day.
As the utility sector evolves to meet the challenges of Net Zero, Smart Metering, Energy Code reform, Market-wide Half-Hourly Settlement, Demand-side Response and Embedded Generation, we combine deep industry knowledge with technical innovation to deliver robust, business-focused solutions backed by dedicated people and exceptional support. We are certified to ISO/IEC 27001:2022, reflecting our commitment to protecting data and managing risk.
The Role
The Head of Cloud Platform Engineering owns the operations and component-level architecture of Flui's AWS cloud estate - the infrastructure that underpins software processing critical market and metering data at national scale. This is a hands-on role: you will design, build and run cloud-native platforms combining AWS-native services with open-source components, and carry end-to-end accountability for how that estate performs, costs, and stands up to scrutiny.
Beyond architecture and operations, you will own FinOps and security for the cloud estate, and act as the accountable owner for its overall fitness for purpose - resilience, performance and scalability - as Flui's platforms scale to support a growing and increasingly complex utility market. You will work closely with the engineering leadership to ensure architecture decisions serve both the product roadmap and the operational realities of running critical infrastructure.
The role suits someone who wants to remain genuinely hands-on with design and build, while holding single-point accountability for how well the cloud estate is run, secured and paid for.
Job Responsibilities
The Head of Cloud Platform Engineering will report to the Technology Director and will be responsible for:
•
Owning the component-level architecture of Flui's AWS cloud estate, spanning AWS-native services and open-source/self-managed components (e.g. container orchestration, messaging, data stores, observability tooling).
•
Operating and continuously improving the platforms underpinning MarketFlow, MeterFlow and DCC adapter, with direct accountability for their resilience, performance and scalability at national-scale transaction volumes.
•
Designing and maintaining disaster recovery, high-availability and capacity plans appropriate to platforms supporting critical utility market infrastructure.
•
Owning FinOps for the cloud estate: cost visibility, forecasting, tagging and allocation, and driving measurable, ongoing cost optimisation without compromising reliability.
•
Owning cloud security posture: identity and access management, network security, encryption, vulnerability and patch management, and ensuring the estate operates in line with Flui's ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and wider compliance obligations.
•
Defining and maintaining the non-functional standards ('fitness for purpose') that platforms must meet - resilience, performance, scalability and observability - and holding engineering teams to them through architecture review and guardrails.
•
Remaining hands-on: designing, building and, where appropriate, personally implementing infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD pipelines and platform tooling alongside the wider engineering team.
•
Owning operational rigor for the estate - incident management, on-call practice, root-cause analysis and continuous improvement of SRE practices.
•
Making and owning build-vs-buy and AWS-native-vs-open-source decisions, balancing cost, control, operability and vendor lock-in.
•
Managing key vendor and technical relationships, including AWS itself and providers of critical open-source or commercial platform tooling.
•
Partnering with the product/engineering leadership to ensure cloud architecture decisions support the product roadmap and time-to-market, and recruiting/developing a small, high-calibre platform engineering team as the estate grows.
•
Championing knowledge sharing and technical education across engineering - documenting architecture decisions and standards, running internal sessions on cloud and platform practice, and mentoring engineers and technical colleagues to raise the wider team's capability.
Essential Competencies and Experience
Business Acumen
•
Demonstrable experience owning cloud platforms supporting a regulated, high-availability or critical-infrastructure business.
•
Ability to balance technical excellence with commercial and operational reality - cost, risk, and delivery pace.
•
Understanding of the utility/energy sector's data and resilience expectations is an advantage.
Cloud Architecture & Platform Engineering
•
Deep, hands-on AWS expertise across compute, storage, networking, data and security services, ideally evidenced by current AWS certification(s).
•
Proven experience designing and operating cloud-native platforms that combine AWS-native services with open-source components (e.g. Kubernetes, Terraform, Kafka or equivalent messaging, Prometheus/Grafana or equivalent observability).
•
Track record of owning a FinOps practice and delivering demonstrable, sustained cloud cost savings.
•
Strong cloud security background - IAM, encryption, vulnerability management - and familiarity with compliance frameworks such as ISO/IEC 27001.
•
Experience defining and meeting non-functional requirements: high availability, disaster recovery, performance/load testing and scalability at production scale.
General
•
Strong infrastructure-as-code skills (Terraform, CloudFormation or CDK) and mature CI/CD practice.
•
Comfortable operating hands-on day to day while also owning strategy, standards and team development.
•
A track record of sharing knowledge and raising technical capability across a team or wider engineering community - through documentation, mentoring, or internal training.
•
Willingness to participate in on-call/incident response as needed for platforms supporting critical services.
Job Qualifications
•
A degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related discipline is a bonus, or equivalent hands-on experience.
•
Current AWS certification(s) - e.g. Solutions Architect Professional, DevOps Engineer Professional or Security Specialty - highly desirable.
Your Personal Characteristics Will Include
•
A pragmatic engineer-leader: hands-on by instinct, comfortable balancing strategic ownership with keyboard time.
•
Security and cost-conscious by default, without losing sight of reliability and delivery speed.
•
Calm and structured under pressure, with a methodical approach to incident response.

·       1-3 years of experience in financial services; experience in asset management is preferred.

·       General knowledge of equity and fixed income investment concepts.
·       Ability to multitask and manage conflicting priorities and workflows within a fast‑paced, globally distributed environment.
·       Strong analytical, organizational, and quality‑control skills, with high attention to detail.
·       Excellent time management and communication skills, with the confidence to engage proactively with global stakeholders.
·       Experience with Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel, and Teams).

Entity and process ownership
